**The three wait layers are DISTINCT — no single configuration is a universal switch.**

| Layer | Mechanism at the pin | Limits that must be preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inner terminal observation (empty `write_stdin`) | Empty-input polls clamp to `[5000, manager cap]`; the manager cap resolves `background_terminal_max_timeout.unwrap_or(300000).max(5000)` (constants `MIN_EMPTY_YIELD_TIME_MS = 5000`, `DEFAULT_MAX_BACKGROUND_TERMINAL_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000` — `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/mod.rs:68-74`; clamp `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs:1029-1043`; resolution `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:4027-4030`; TOML field `codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs:345-347`) | The cap is an UPPER BOUND — a long observation still requires an explicit long `yield_time_ms`; an omitted yield is ≈5000 ms (the argument's 250-ms default is clamped up — `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/write_stdin.rs:23-32`). Non-empty writes stay ≤30000 ms and the first `exec_command` yield clamps to `[250, 30000]` ms (Windows floor 10000) regardless of config (`codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/mod.rs:212-218`). Raising the cap alone lengthens nothing: the production Skill's 60000-ms window does not become an hour by raising the cap alone |
| Outer code-mode cell | `features.code_mode.default_exec_yield_time_ms` (`codex-rs/features/src/feature_configs.rs:36-43`) is the wait filled into exec requests WITHOUT an explicit pragma — core default 30000 ms (`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:1200,1219`; resolution `:2778-2792`; filled via `get_or_insert`, `codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:130-135`). The protocol's bare 10000-ms constants are NOT the effective core default (`codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/runtime.rs:15-16`). In the examined core-default paths there is NO fixed 30-second outer hard cap: the runtime applies `min()` only against a session-EXPLICIT `max_yield_time_ms` (`codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/service.rs:29,71,140,201`) | An explicit shorter `@exec` pragma wins over the configured default; an ALREADY-YIELDED cell's outer `wait` has its own independent 10000-ms default and does NOT read the exec default (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/wait_handler.rs:30,37-39,134-141`); an active explicit yield, user input/preempt, resource limits, cancellation and REAL JS completion can each return earlier than any configured window (ordinary output buffers do not end the observation; only the `Result`-terminated completion path does — `codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/execute_handler.rs:135,146-147`) |
| Root-for-Child V2 wait | `features.multi_agent_v2.default_wait_timeout_ms` with min/max — source defaults 30000 / 10000 / 3600000 ms (`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:257-264`; struct `:1369`; validation `:3957-3992`); the V2 wait handler reads them from the per-turn config (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/wait.rs:53`) | A Child's long wait says nothing about the Root not waking early: mailbox/user-input activity can wake the wait before the deadline (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/wait.rs:213-220`). The machine's ACTUAL runtime configuration was NOT read this round — only source defaults are recorded |

**Inheritance is config-real, not prompt-only.** The inner cap and the code-mode default reach the
actual Child through the full parent effective-`Config` clone — `build_agent_shared_config` starts
from `turn.config.clone()` (`codex-rs/core/src/agent/child_config.rs:110-164`; the same clone-based
helper serves fresh spawn and resume) — and the Child session constructs its terminal manager and
code-mode service from that config: `UnifiedExecProcessManager::new(config.background_terminal_max_timeout)`
(`codex-rs/core/src/session/session.rs:1725-1732`) and `CodeModeService::new(…, &config.code_mode, …)`,
which copies `default_exec_yield_time_ms` into the service field
(`codex-rs/core/src/session/session.rs:1818-1823`; `codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:86-103`).
The two keys are NOT in the Role typed whitelist (`codex-rs/core/src/agent/role.rs:36-47`) — adding
arbitrary fields to a Role file does not achieve a Role-scoped override. Loaded sessions do not
hot-reload: an already-loaded Child is reused as-is, and an owner-validated reload builds a NEW
Session from a fresh clone — a running service never picks up config-file edits automatically.

**The outer default is NOT new.** It was introduced 2026-08-07 by
`d0c8f422eaaa40b3927b43a0fff7e753e8514f34` ("Configure the default code-mode exec yield timeout
(#37352)", 2026-08-07T01:41:54Z), which is an ancestor of the OLD pin `67727e7c…` (verified by
merge-base), so the executed campaign's own source pin already contained it. Correct framing: a
PREVIOUSLY UNDER-EXPLOITED/UNDER-VERIFIED entry point whose verification coverage should be filled
in — never "the host only now supports long waits".

**The genuine default change is interruption.** `72c959528ee4ca74abdb8575fbbc4e36960a8c47`
(2026-10-07, "Enable code mode interruption by default (#51835)") flipped `code_mode_interrupt` from
UnderDevelopment/default-false to Stable/default-true (`codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs:1197-1202` at
`dffa0deb…`; the old pin records `Stage::UnderDevelopment` / `default_enabled: false` at
`codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs:1103-1108`). Consequence chain at the new pin: the turn-abort path
awaits `interrupt_active_cells()` when the abort reason is `Interrupted` AND the feature is enabled
(`codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs:960-971`), which terminates each active code-mode cell
(`codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:164-178`) and cancels nested pending tool futures — so a
native Interrupt, or an exact-Child `interrupt_agent`, need not wait out a long observation window.
Boundaries that survive: this does NOT auto-clear the terminal process store (a cancelled poll future
releases only its own process clone; the terminate-all path is the separate clean/shutdown route); it
is NOT Companion-process stop, ZCode-job stop or durable settlement — the plugin's exact
stop/reconciliation/no-collateral-cancellation contract still needs its own verification; and the
interrupt tool's `previous_status` is a PRE-interruption status snapshot, not a completion
confirmation (consistent with §13.5's recording).

**Token framing (mechanism only; nothing measured).** The source turn loop awaits the drain of
in-flight tool futures within one sampling (`codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs:2565,3280`) — there is
no wall-clock re-sampling that restarts the model on a timer. Shortened observations that return to
the model add repeat decision/sampling opportunities, so lengthened windows have a MECHANISTIC BASIS
for fewer repeat samplings — and nothing more: no whole-task-zero-token claim, no infinite-wait
claim, no percentage-savings claim.

**Priority framing.** The 0.162.1 campaign's `unsupported-call-shape` outcome (§13.4–§13.6) was
INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — it is not evidence that the host removed or lacks long-wait capability, and
the shell route must not be concluded infeasible from the inconclusive. The sensible next sequence
(as the source investigation itself recommends): first confirm the installed host's two-layer
effective configuration and interruption capability, and resolve the probe recognition boundary
(§13.10's Path A candidate); only then consider small-scale verification. This section authorizes no
production Skill/Role/config change (spec S7; §13.10's delivery boundary).

2. `S-binding` — changed result binding: `const q = …; text(q);` (binding spelling varies; identical
   syntax relations; retained facts must be identical apart from the existing sanctioned
   digest/envelope AND apart from the `parserStage` diagnosis — the existing grammar pins the `r`
   spelling (WRAPPER_PATTERN, evidence.mjs:49), so a changed binding necessarily reports the wrapper
   stage, exactly as the plan's Task 2 example asserts via `parseCallStatements(…) === null` for a
   noncanonical binding; no binding-spelling-dependent syntax/decision fact exists).
3. `S-tail-missing` — missing emission tail: first statement only.
4. `S-tail-changed` — changed emission tail: `text(JSON.stringify(r));` or `text(r.status);`.
5. `S-arg-unsupported` — unsupported argument expression: `{cmd: buildCmd()}` or spread.
6. `S-string-contained` — tool-like text inside a private literal: `cmd:"prep text(r) tools.exec_command
   (prompt) alias"`; lexer boundaries first, so NO syntax fact may be derived from that content.
7. `S-extra` — extra hidden statement: a third plausible statement after the accepted pair.
8. `S-trailing-blank` — trailing blank formatting after the final statement (`;\n\n`, trailing blanks).

**Closed decision dimensions (each alternative is expected to differ on a specific subset; one
dimension per existing failure family):** whole-wrapper mismatch (head class + whole-body coverage);
argument decoding rejection (literal-object vs unsupported vs over-limit); output projection (tail
class); extra/unresolved content (residual statements / trailing formatting / slot-limit); lexical
state (complete vs unterminated vs unsupported syntax); parser stage (which existing stage rejects);
directive state (absent/valid/invalid/unknown); tool family (`exec_command` vs other). These dimensions
are the Task 1-frozen discriminator set; the classifier reports closed enums ONLY.

**FROZEN diagnostic schema v1 (`inspectCallShape` — Task 2 implements exactly this; local
investigation decision under plan §2 privacy contract).** A pure, non-evaluating static classifier over
the raw call string; fixed input bounds: byte length ≤ 8192 (UTF-8), ≤ 16 statement slots, argument
literal ≤ 4096 chars (matches `MAX_WRAPPER_ARGUMENT_CHARS`); excerpt/diagnostic record still bounded by
the existing 2048-char budget. Truncated input NEVER becomes success; a fact that cannot be established
inside these bounds is dropped whole with an incomplete marker.

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "coverage": "complete | partial | over-budget | over-scope",   // classification coverage ONLY, never admission
  "statements": [ {                                              // ≤16 nodes; dropped whole (with statementCount retained) when unsayable
      "head":       "bound-await | bare-await | emission | other | unknown",
      "tool":       "exec_command | other | no-call | unknown",    // allowlist = {"exec_command"}; any other established name, incl. spelling, is "other"; unknown only when lexical state blocks classification
      "argument":   "literal-object | unsupported | none | over-limit",
      "lexical":    "complete | unterminated | invalid | unsupported-syntax",
      "tail":       "text-binding | text-stringify-binding | text-public-field | text-other | none | unknown"
  } ],
  "statementCount":   "<integer 0..16> | over-limit",
  "tool":             "exec_command | other | no-call | unknown", // top-level mirror: tool class of the LAST call-carrying statement ('no-call' when none)
  "head":             "bound-await | bare-await | emission | other | unknown",  // top-level mirror: FIRST statement's head
  "tail":             "text-binding | text-stringify-binding | text-public-field | text-other | none | unknown",  // top-level mirror: LAST statement's tail
  "bindingEquality":  "equal | not-equal | unrelated | unknown", // head binding identifier == tail emission identifier (equality only; spelling never retained)
  "parserStage":      "parse-accepted | wrapper | arguments | output | residual | directive | unknown",  // existing-parser stage order (diagnosis only)
  "directive":        "absent | valid | invalid | unknown",      // directive verdict read from the existing parseCallEvent directive readback; keys never retained
  "wholeInputConsumed": <boolean>                                // classification coverage only
}
```

**Schema v1 amendment (close-out correction, 2026-10-17, user-commissioned two-axis review;
adjudicated — the frozen block above is NOT rewritten).** One record-budget retention field joins
the PROJECTED shape block, quoted field line:

```jsonc
  "retention": "full | partial",   // record-budget serialization marker: 'partial' when any fact was dropped for the excerpt budget ('statements' array or everything), 'full' when every fact was serialized — NEVER a classification verdict
```

It describes SERIALIZATION only — `coverage`/`wholeInputConsumed` keep describing CLASSIFICATION
and are unchanged in every tier. The projector sets it on every tier and budgets it with them:
full facts → `retention: 'full'`; the `statements`-dropped tier → `retention: 'partial'`;
and the minimal marker becomes `{ "version": 1, "coverage": "over-budget", "retention":
"partial" }` — the redundant `wholeInputConsumed` field is OMITTED there ('over-budget' always
means `false`, so the classification meaning is unchanged) because the tightest observed tier
budget (67 serialized characters at sixteen slots — 2048 − baseJson 296 − diagnosticJson 1662 −
23 separator characters, re-derived from the projector's own formula) otherwise could not hold
both the marker and the retention field; when even the 60-character marker does not fit, the
block is omitted
entirely (no unmarked partial result exists). Provenance: the evidence.mjs byte change flows
into the observer digest automatically (designed behavior).

Retains-a-count note (plan §2 anchoring): beyond booleans/enums, the ONLY new count-like facts are
`statementCount` and the `statements` array length — both directly represent the schema-projected
syntax tree's fixed statement-slot count, which plan §2 expressly allows ("fixed public node kinds,
fixed child slots and binding-equality relations, at most 64 nodes/depth 8/16 statement slots"); no
other numeric series (string lengths, source offsets, per-token counts) is retained.

Field semantics fixed at freeze: `head` from the first significant token class (declaration-binding of
an await → `bound-await`; bare await statement → `bare-await`; emission-first (`text(…)` as its own
head) → `emission`; anything else → `other`/`unknown`). `tail` 'value' classes: `text(<result binding
identifier>)` → `text-binding`; `text(JSON.stringify(<identifier>))` → `text-stringify-binding`;
`text(<identifier>.<allowlisted public result field>)` → `text-public-field` (allowlist table is EMPTY
at v1 — no public field is enumerated, so any property projection stays `text-other`; extending it
requires a new adjudication); anything else inside `text(…)` → `text-other`; no emission → `none`.
`tail` at top level mirrors the LAST statement's tail; top-level `tool` and `head` are the remaining
mirror fields the plan's Task 2 example pins — top-level `tool` is the tool class of the LAST
call-carrying statement (`no-call` when none), top-level `head` mirrors the FIRST statement's head —
so the plan's single-call example (`const alias = await …; text(alias);`) projects
`head: bound-await`, `tool: exec_command`, `tail: text-binding` with no binding spelling retained.
`bindingEquality` compares only identifier
equality between an earlier statement's bound result and the final emission's argument identifier — no
name retained (the plan's example asserts `JSON.stringify(facts)` does not contain `alias`). Public
syntax strings (`exec_command`, `text(`, `JSON.stringify`) exist ONLY as fixed enum labels. Lexical
state unsupported features (template literals, regex literals, class fields, optional chaining, etc.)
map the affected statement to `lexical: unsupported-syntax` and `head/tool: unknown` — never probed
further. Statement slot order: lexical string/comment boundaries are applied BEFORE structural
classification, so tool-like text inside task strings never produces `tool` facts. `parserStage`
mirrors the classification order of existing `parseCallStatements` stages (wrapper → arguments →
output → residual → directive); `parse-accepted` is a diagnosis report of that parser's response, NOT
an admission verdict and NEVER a fake validated-call object (`parseCallStatements`' own null/parsed
outcome stays pinned separately as the plan's example requires). Directive state read from the
in-memory `parseCallEvent` directive value with the existing private-key withholding; errors →
`unknown`.

**Interpretive decisions as implemented (schema corners the frozen block leaves open; flagged for
the D0 adjudication, not silently).** (a) Non-string input returns the fixed out-of-scope result
`{version:1, coverage:'over-scope', statements:[], statementCount:0, tool:'no-call', head:'unknown',
tail:'none', bindingEquality:'unknown', parserStage:'unknown', directive:'unknown',
wholeInputConsumed:false}` — the schema has no invalid-input member, so "over-scope" reads as
outside the classifier's scope. (b) Record-budget overflow of the excerpt projection reuses
`coverage:'over-budget'` on the minimal marker — the incomplete marker semantics, not a new enum
member. (c) Statement slots are NEWLINE slots (mirroring the existing per-line cell splitter), so
the wrapper+emission pair on ONE line is ONE schema node carrying both head and tail — this is what
lets the plan's single-line example project `head:'bound-await'`/`tail:'text-binding'` as pinned.
(d) `parserStage` is the mechanical RAW-line mirror of the existing grammar (e.g. raw control
characters inside a JSON string literal reject the decode → 'arguments'; lexically broken lines →
'wrapper'), which can differ from the string-boundary-aware statement facts by design: the facts
describe the shape, the stage diagnoses the parser's response. (e) Trailing blank formatting keeps
every statement fact identical to the canonical control and diverges only on
`parserStage:'residual'` (the existing grammar rejects a blank line after the last statement).

**Canonical-exact design evaluation (root adjudication requested; NOT redesigned this round).**
After nine rounds of carried-context corners, a "canonical-exact recognition + everything
non-canonical unknown/partial" design would likely be a SIMPLER TERMINATING SHAPE: pros — one
positive grammar (the pinned wrapper/inline/preparation/root-control patterns already exist),
every non-match falls to a single unknown/partial path (no carried-context matrix to grow), the
frozen 8-record set is fully discriminated by exactly that grammar, and the review surface
shrinks from ~20 boundary helpers to pattern-conjunction checks; cons — the current classifier
additionally answers questions the canonical grammar cannot (e.g. distinguishing an
unsupported-argument wrapper from a foreign statement, the trivia-tolerant `text (r)` emission,
and per-statement head/tail classes for partial cells), so a naive collapse would lose that
diagnostic richness unless the unknown path also carried a small coarse-fact block (statement
count, byte class, await presence); effort — a focused rewrite of `classifyStatementSlot` +
`diagnoseParserStage` (~200 lines) plus re-pinning ~30 of the 80 focused tests, est. one session.
Root's call; the current design remains within contract.

**Canonical-exact redesign (round 10 adjudication, EXECUTED; 2026-10-16, same amended task
commit).** After codex round 10 returned four more P2 findings (stable ~4/round, all living in the
classifier's carried-context/boundary-helper web), the root adjudicated the redesign this
evaluation paragraph anticipated, a first attempt was abandoned mid-rewrite and rolled back
cleanly, and this rewrite was executed at full capacity. ARCHITECTURE: positive recognition is now
the pinned grammar mirrors ALONE — every statement slot is segmented at top-level `;`/`}`
boundaries over the string/comment-masked code (the lexer `lexCellLines`/`lexCellLine` is kept
verbatim), and EVERY segment must match one explicit positive statement form anchored in a proven
statement position; the positive forms are the frozen 8-record discrimination set expressed as
direct mechanical variants of the verbatim WRAPPER/INLINE mirrors (generalized binding
identifier, missing tail, changed tail incl. `text(JSON.stringify(r))`/`text(r.<prop>)`,
unsupported argument form, extra statement, trailing blank formatting), the trivia-tolerant
emission (`text\s*\(` — masked comments ARE trivia), and the awaited-call statement (the wrapper
skeleton without the binding prefix, required by the split-declaration and comma-declarator
variants); the mechanical parser-stage mirror (`diagnoseParserStage` and its raw-line helpers) is
kept verbatim as variant (c). EVERYTHING ELSE collapses into ONE conservative unknown path BY
CONSTRUCTION — a non-matching segment, a `tools`/`text` token (exact identifier boundaries,
surrogate-pair exact) outside a pinned position, any backslash escape in code position, a slot
inside a spanning bracket construct, or an unproven statement position classifies the whole slot
unknown (head/tool 'unknown', coverage 'partial', wholeInputConsumed false, bindingEquality
'unknown') — which is what DELETES the boundary-helper web wholesale (eleven helpers:
`identifierContinuationBefore`, `precededByUnicodeEscape`, `containsIdentifierStartEscape`,
`followsPrivateExpression`, `maskedEndsWithSignificantDot`, `maskedEndsWithIdentifierNew`,
`maskedEndsWithSplitToolReference`, `maskedEndsWithSplitEmissionReference`,
`pendingDeclarationIdentifier`, `provenCallPosition`, `publicPositionTriviaSplitToolReference`,
plus `depthBefore`, `completeToolCalls`, `outermostEmissionIndex`, `precededByFunctionKeyword`,
`precededByNewKeyword`; only the trivial `maskedEndsWithStatementBoundary` survives as the
carried proven-start bit). The frozen schema v1 is UNCHANGED (same enums, bounds, mirrors,
budget projection, truncation-never-success); evidence.mjs/driver.mjs interfaces stay as-is;
provenance digest v2 bytes changed automatically with the helper rewrite (designed behavior,
pinned by the negative-control tests). ROUND-10 CLASSES, CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION, EACH PINNED AS
A TEST: (i) `const _r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"x"}); text(_r);` binds normally — `$` and
`_` are ECMAScript identifier-start characters NOT inside `\p{ID_Start}` (the low line U+005F is
a separate property), so the identifier classes spell both out; head 'bound-await', tail
'text-binding', bindingEquality 'equal', coverage 'complete' (test 'an underscore-initial binding
is an ordinary JavaScript identifier (round 10, class i)'; the pre-redesign classifier reported
head 'other'/tail 'text-other'/'unrelated' — a genuine defect); (ii) `const r =\n0; await
tools.exec_command({cmd:"x"}); text(r);` — the pending declaration is adopted ONLY when the
continuation slot itself STARTS the awaited initializer, so the split layout reports
'unrelated', AGREEING with the joined `const r = 0; …` layout (test 'a pending declaration is
adopted only when the continuation starts the awaited initializer (round 10, class ii)';
pre-redesign: 'equal' vs joined 'unrelated' — a layout disagreement defect); (iii) `const r =
await tools.exec_command({cmd:"x"}), s = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"y"}); text(s);` —
comma-separated declarators are handled POSITIONALLY (the last awaited binding before the final
emission binds it): both layouts 'equal' (test 'comma-separated declarators bind positionally
like the split layout (round 10, class iii)'; pre-redesign: 'not-equal' vs split 'equal'); (iv)
an identifier escape ANYWHERE inside a reference token (`await \u0074ools.exec_command(…)`,
`await tools.exec_comman\u0064(…)`, `privat\u{65}tools…`) withholds the slot unknown/partial —
never a confident presence OR absence (test 'an identifier escape anywhere in a reference token
withholds the slot (round 10, class iv)'; pre-redesign: the escape-at-end form persisted a
confident 'no-call' under COMPLETE coverage — the over-reporting defect class all ten rounds
kept finding). EIGHT-RECORD + PARSER-STAGE NON-COARSENING, VERIFIED EXPLICITLY: records 1-8
re-verified at this commit with FULL fact-set equality against the frozen expectations (record 1
canonical 'parse-accepted'/'equal' deep-equal; record 2 identical facts except parserStage
'wrapper'; record 3 'output'/'none'/'unrelated'; record 4 stringify canonical and property
'text-other'/'output'/'equal'; record 5 'unsupported' at the 'arguments' stage; record 6
fact-identical to the canonical control AND still accepted by the real parser; record 7 'other'
statement at 'residual' with 'equal'; record 8 residual-stage-only divergence), and the
`parserStage` ⇔ `parseCallStatements` agreement holds over all 12 pinned inputs. COARSENING
DISCLOSURES (per item; every affected existing test re-pinned to the honest new expectation —
each is the plan's "smallest finite classifier" + honest-unknown semantics doing exactly what
they sanction: a public syntax fact the canonical grammar cannot positively recognize is no
longer asserted): (1) same-line member-receiver emission `obj.text(r)` — was tail 'none'/
'unrelated' under complete coverage, now the slot withholds unknown/partial (test 'public syntax
facts require COMPLETE tool and emission references'); (2) trivia-after-dot references `obj.
tools.…`/`obj. text(…)` — was 'no-call'/'none', now withheld unknown/partial (test
'complete-reference checks skip trivia and honor Unicode identifier continuations'; the
Unicode-continuation `πtools` case KEEPS its precise 'no-call' — it is a single identifier, so
the token scan is reliably decidable); (3) cross-line member chains `obj.\ntools.…`,
`obj.\n  tools.…`, `obj.\ntext(r);`, and the comment-line-carried variant — was
'no-call'/'none' under complete coverage, now withheld unknown/partial (tests 'reference
boundaries carry across newline slots', 'member-reference context survives leading trivia and
trivia-only lines'); (4) identifier-escape references `privat\u{65}tools…`/`…privat\u{65}text(r)`
— was 'no-call'/'none', now withheld (round-10 class iv; test 'identifier escapes keep
references private'); (5) function/generator declarations, method definitions and constructor
invocations carrying the emission token (`function text(r) {}`, `function* text(r) {}`,
`{text(r) {}}` incl. the spanning-object case, `new text(r);`, `new\ntext(r);`) — was tail
'none' under complete coverage, now withheld unknown/partial; the safety property (these never
establish an emission) is now true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by exclusion lists (tests
'declarations and method definitions are not emission calls', 'generators, constructors and
unproven contexts are not emission calls', 'per-line emission depth is cell-relative across
spanning objects' — the spanning case additionally coarsens bindingEquality 'equal'→'unknown'
and coverage 'complete'→'partial' because unclassified slots follow the final emission); (6)
unproven-position assignments (`const assigned = text(other);`) — tail/relation stay 'unknown'
but coverage coarsens 'complete'→'partial' (test 'uncertainty precedes identifier equality
regardless of slot layout'); (7) private-name class bodies (`this.#tools.…`) — was 'no-call'
under complete coverage, now withheld unknown/partial (test 'private-name suffixes never
establish the public tool reference'); (8) escaped await continuations (`await\u0061`) — was
head 'other'/'unrelated', now withheld 'unknown' (test 'escaped identifier continuations after
await are not the keyword'; the `await$secret`/`awaitπ` cases KEEP their precise 'other' heads —
token-boundary failures are decidable without escapes); (9) the trivia-split and cross-line
split reference slots keep their unknown classification but the slot's LEXICAL verdict is now
the lexer's honest 'complete' (the withhold is a classification verdict, not a broken-lexical
verdict — the old 'unsupported-syntax' label on lexically sound lines is retired) in tests 'a
trivia-split tool reference is unknown-classified, never a no-call claim', 'a tool reference
split across newline slots is unknown-classified, never a confident no-call', 'an emission
reference split across a newline slot withholds the relation', 'unsupported references relabel a
slot even when a canonical call shares it', 'escaped references in reference position are
unknown-classified'; (10) `await tools.工具({});` KEEPS its recognized 'other' call class
(Unicode tool names are inside the pinned call form); the astral `𐐀tools` case KEEPS its precise
'no-call' (𐐀 is ID_Start ⊂ ID_Continue, so `𐐀tools` is one identifier — no re-pin needed).

**The existing stop trigger induced by native Child interruption, and obligation convergence WITHOUT a
second stop authority (worktree trace).** The ONLY stop the delivered interrupt induces is the HOST-side
chain above: exact-Child turn abort + active-cell termination. At the plugin layer, a native Child turn
interruption creates NO stop cause: `stopCauseFor` (`scripts/lib/rescue-lifecycle.mjs:114-122`) grants
stop authority ONLY to (a) an explicit stop intent (`intent.kind === 'stop'`, with Host Coordination
Loss restricted to attached foreground work), (b) a SessionEnd receipt matching the job's owning
lifecycle epoch (`:119`), or (c) attached-foreground host-coordination loss (`:120`, gate `:134-137`).
A delivered-but-foreign-origin interrupt is none of these, so NO durable stop intent is persisted by
the interrupt itself and no job is explicitly cancelled through a different authority. The plugin's
obligations converge only through the EXISTING paths: observation passes stay bounded
(`observeSettle`, rescue-lifecycle.mjs:597); the worker's natural completion publishes `succeeded`
through the natural-terminal branch after the gated runner cleanup
(`settleRemoteEvidence` :253-261 → `runRunnerCleanup` :459-471 → `cleanupAllowsSettlement` :485-487);
a real stop cause later persists the durable stop intent FIRST and settles remote evidence in the
mandated order (`stopAndSettle` :154-195; first-level `interrupted` classification publishes
`cancelled` behind the gated cleanup :273-292); every uncertain outcome retains the writable guard.
The interrupt tool's `previous_status` is a PRE-interruption snapshot (source :74-76), never
settlement. Companion-side interruption detection exists only as evidence decoding:
`extractInterruptInteraction` (evidence.mjs:1526) classifies the V2 interaction through

### 16.3 Frozen safe observation sequence (preregistered for I1; all stages mandatory)

Every stage's timestamps ride the held-turn monotonic clock (`held-turn-monotonic-elapsed-ms`,
driver.mjs:971-980) for probe-side events and attributable rollout event timestamps for host-side
events; a value that cannot be established stays `null`/unknown, never zero. Target identity prefers
the ACTUAL spawn id; if the host exposes only an alias, resolution happens ONLY through the supported
authoritative runtime mapping (the launch acknowledgement's own returned identifier in the rollout);
alias spelling or caller claims never substitute, and a missing mapping keeps target attribution
unknown.

1. **Exact target / spawn acknowledgement** — the exact managed Child's launch observed through
   `waitForLauncherObservation` (driver.mjs:2089) and the launch output's own returned Child
   identifier (session/agent id namespace as the host returns it), one mapped launch/send
   (`companionLaunchCount`/`companionSendCount`), original handle grounded from the launch's own
   statement-position output (driver.mjs:2153-2178).
2. **Pending poll event/window** — `waitForPollObservation` (driver.mjs:2136) records the decisive
   empty-input original-handle poll and its start on the monotonic timeline
   (`pollStartedAtElapsedMs`); the pending interval is [poll start, poll resolution) and delivery must
   occur strictly inside it, before natural completion.
3. **Delivered native interaction** — `interrupt_agent` to the EXACT running Child id only;
   `extractInterruptInteraction` (evidence.mjs:1526) records attempted/delivered/`previousStatus`/
   target-suppression and the call's attributable bounds (`callAtMs`, `notBeforeMs`/`notAfterMs`,
   evidence.mjs:1599-1619); wrong target, unresolved alias, terminal-before-interrupt, or
   delivery-unsent all fail the case (no fallback interaction).
4. **Cell / poll settlement** — the bound pending observation resolves (terminate response /
   cancelled future / a later bound response per evidence.mjs:1535-1597); settlement is recorded with
   its own attributable timestamp, and delivery-to-settlement latency is measured on the one monotonic
   clock against the §16.5 oracle bound.
5. **Companion liveness** — the exact attached Companion/worker process outcome recorded SEPARATELY
   (ceased / correct terminal result / survived) via the existing verified-process identity machinery
   and `waitForChildSettlementObservation` (driver.mjs:2228); never inferred from `previous_status`,
   a Root final message, gate release or later disposal.
6. **Exact durable job / stop intent / terminal winner** — read through the existing bounded state
   adapters: the exact job record, whether a durable stop intent exists (none may exist unless a real
   stop authority acted), and the terminal winner exactly as published (or explicitly pending).
7. **Writable-guard / executor obligations** — the writable guard/exclusion and executor-route
   obligations' settled/unsettled status recorded separately through the existing recovery/state
   adapters, each never collapsed into another layer's outcome.

### 16.4 Declared unrelated survival control for I1 (concrete design; Task 2 implements + tests)

**Design: root-side independent progress-terminal control.** Within the SAME I1 fixture home and the
SAME held Root turn lifecycle, and declared in the case registration BEFORE the host launch, the held
Root turn starts ONE additional harmless background command through the ordinary `exec_command` seam
on its OWN handle: a fixture-owned bounded script emitting exactly 30 unique progress lines
(`zcode-survival-control <line-index> <monotonic-tag>`) at a fixed 2000-ms cadence (~60 s total) and
then exiting 0 naturally. It never touches the observed Companion handle, is not a Rescue Child, and
shares no job/guard/lease state with the plugin.

**Why it cannot share the interrupt's stop authority (source-proven):** the delivered interaction
targets the exact Child agent id; the interrupt chain (§16.2) aborts the CHILD's turn and terminates
the CHILD session's active cells, and never calls the terminate-all route — the ROOT's own terminal
process store is unreachable from it. A cancelled poll future releases only its own clone
(process_manager.rs:479-491), so even the control's own observation cell being later ended by turn
cleanup cannot stop the control process; fixture disposal's clean/shutdown route happens only after
evidence capture and is recorded as cleanup, never as survival evidence. Rejected alternative
(recorded): a second V2 spawned agent in the same Root — closer by family, but it shares the V2 agent
registry and targeting surface and needs spawn/registration seams the fixture does not have; the
root-side terminal control is smaller and provably outside the interrupt authority.

**Positive activity before/at delivery:** immediately BEFORE delivering the interrupt, the held turn
issues one bounded read on the control's own handle and REQUIRES a fresh progress line whose
line-index advanced (index k with k < 30, so the control is provably mid-run — an already-completed
control, last index 30, fails no-collateral qualification) and whose read event precedes the interrupt
call event in the bound rollout ordering (the same ordering machinery as §16.2's evidence decode).
**After delivery (codex round-1 revision, 2026-10-18 — survival binds to EMISSION time, never to
observation time):** one further bounded read after the interrupt's settlement evidence is NECESSARY
but never SUFFICIENT: a post-delivery observation proves nothing about WHEN the bytes were written, so
a control that emitted a line before delivery and died during delivery would still leave that line
readable afterward. Qualification therefore requires the control's progress lines to carry a monotonic
emission tag/timestamp written by the control itself AT EMIT TIME, and continued liveness is proven
ONLY by a line whose EMISSION tag falls strictly AFTER the recorded delivery bound (the delivered
interaction's attributable timestamp per §16.3 stage 3); independent natural completion is likewise
proven ONLY by the completion marker's OWN emission time after that same delivery bound — never by the
post-delivery read/exit-result event timestamp, the observation's rollout event time, or the read
ordering alone. Unknown/unreadable post-delivery state, no post-delivery evidence, or no emission tag
establishable after the delivery bound keeps no-collateral NOT qualified. Synthetic source/unit
assurances never substitute. Projected facts are closed whitelisted fields only (started /
lastLineIndexAtDelivery / lastEmissionTagBeforeDelivery /
activityAtDelivery ∈ {active, completed-before, unknown} / postDelivery ∈ {alive, completed, lost,
unknown} / postDeliveryEmissionTag with its strict-after-delivery-bound comparison + attributable
timestamps); the selector is a single closed value valid ONLY for `rescue-interrupt`; command bytes
are fixture-owned, never caller-supplied (no arbitrary argv/config bag). This is NEW finite Task 2
surface with RED→GREEN validation and privacy tests, which MUST include the buffered-output negative
regressions BEFORE this oracle freezes: (a) a control whose lines were ALL emitted before delivery —
even when a post-delivery read returns them — does NOT qualify no-collateral; (b) a control whose
last line was emitted before delivery and which died during delivery is REJECTED even though the
post-delivery read returns its buffered bytes; (c) a completion whose marker emission time cannot be
established after the delivery bound keeps survival NOT qualified.

**Readiness-coordination revision (2026-10-18, post-F codex review fix — research-only correction
for the record; NO new interrupt launch follows).** The F-registered sequencing (§17.11) asked Root
to deliver and observe the CHILD's long empty-input `write_stdin` as its first step. That step was
architecturally impossible and is removed: process handles and pending cells belong to the Child's
session, and Root's tools cannot operate on them. The child's long poll stays CHILD-OWNED, driven by
the child's own registered candidate paragraph (byte-identical, unchanged). The registered
rescue-interrupt flow is corrected to five strictly ordered steps, all through Root's OWN supported
tools: (A) spawn the Rescue child exactly as before and retain the spawn acknowledgement's EXACT
full agent id; (B) IMMEDIATELY AFTER the child launch, launch the bounded control ONCE on its OWN
`exec_command` handle (never the child's handle, never Status, never stop/kill) so its designed
lifetime covers the delivery coordination; (C) readiness coordination through the control clock —
bounded empty-input reads (`yield_time_ms` 1000), each requiring a fresh line, until a line whose
index is at least **40** (the readiness floor ≈ 80 seconds after control start at the 2000-ms
cadence) is observed; (D) the §16.4 pre-delivery read (one more fresh mid-run read ordered before
the interrupt); (E) the exactly-one `interrupt_agent` call carrying the EXACT full agent id from the
spawn acknowledgement — never shortened, paraphrased, or guessed. The control design extends from 30
lines (~60 s) to **60 lines at the same fixed 2000-ms cadence (~120 s designed lifetime; designed
exit code 0, tag semantics and the lineCount-driven premature/abnormal-exit classification
unchanged)**, sized to cover the recorded child poll-start latency (R 57623 ms, L 68044 ms, F 72069
ms elapsed — roughly 57.6–72.1 s) with coordination margin; the declared fixture script digest
changes accordingly for any FUTURE registered run (no live run is re-registered — §16.7's recorded
digests remain the historical record of the runs they registered). The readiness floor is an
**OBSERVER-COORDINATION APPROXIMATION** of the child's poll-start window, recorded as such — it is
NOT a claim of observing the child's poll (which Root cannot observe except through the recorded
host timeline, and never drives). All prior prohibitions stand: the control is unrelated to the
Rescue child (do not confuse the two handles, do not interrupt it), never Status-observed, never
sent input, never stopped or killed; the after-settlement read is still reported verbatim. This
correction follows the two P2 codex review findings on the post-F range (Root cannot satisfy a
child-handle prerequisite; a control whose lifetime can expire before preparation completes
guarantees the §16.4 pre-delivery read sees a completed control). **No new interrupt launch
follows:** I1 and F are the only interrupt launches and both are spent (§17.13); Gate D remains
precisely BLOCKED with the measured §17.12 blocker; the registered case is corrected for the record
only.

### 16.5 Preregistered responsiveness oracle (before any I1 launch)

**No applicable measured native-interrupt baseline exists.** Every prior interrupt-bearing run ended
inconclusive BEFORE delivery (§7.7, §13.5), so there is no delivery-to-settlement measurement to
reuse; C0's 31007-ms pending yield (§15.5) and D0's 97500-ms pending poll (§15.3) measure the YIELD
path, not interrupt settlement — they are context, not a latency baseline. I0 remains the one
conditional label (plan §3) if Task 4 judges the composition-derived bound below insufficient; a
control that missed its pending window is not a latency baseline, and a wait-until-the-hour-ends
outcome is never "responsive".

**Production has NO aggregate delivery-to-settlement deadline.** The bounded existing-stage
composition, from configured values only:

| Stage | Existing configured bound | Source/production cite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host delivery (interrupt_agent → Op::Interrupt) | no configured numeric bound at the pin (in-process registry send) — UNKNOWN, recorded unknown | interrupt_agent.rs:33-77; control.rs:330-341 |
| Child turn-abort grace before forced task abort | 100 ms (`GRACEFULL_INTERRUPTION_TIMEOUT_MS`) | tasks/mod.rs:72, :979-984 |
| Active-cell termination (pending poll future cancellation) | no configured numeric bound at the pin — UNKNOWN, recorded unknown | code_mode/mod.rs:164-178 |
| Plugin-side stop/reconcile passes (only if a real stop cause exists) | marked-runner termination ≤ 750 ms per pass (non-Windows; min 50; Windows 1500/6000, duty fallback 30000); lock timeouts 30000 ms; broker lookup 250 ms | job-control.mjs:26, :38-72, :121, :138 |
| Status observation (if used to observe, never to settle) | caller-supplied explicit `--timeout-ms`, `JOB_WAIT_TIMEOUT` at expiry; production 120000-ms deadline confirmed firing un-extended (§13.7) | job-control.mjs:967-968 |

**Preregistered bound (Task 4 measures against this; no production timeout is changed):**
delivery-to-settlement for the native turn/cell/poll layer is RESPONSIVE only if the attributable
settlement evidence (§16.3 stage 4) is observed within **60000 ms** of the delivered interaction's
attributable delivery bound — 1/60 of the 3600000-ms candidate window, ~1/7 of the 420000-ms hold,
~600× the host's own 100-ms abort grace so ordinary transport overhead cannot false-negative, and on
the same scale as I0's 60000-ms window so I0 and I1 are directly comparable. An observation with no
settlement by 60000 ms is recorded NOT responsive (bound exceeded) — never retried into
responsiveness, and never measured from the window's end instead of the delivery point. The
Companion, durable-job/guard and no-collateral layers keep their own separate §16.3 stage outcomes and
are never folded into this latency.

- **Gate A (actual route / authority): PASS — scoped to the records whose facts support it

  linkage, exactly one mapped launch/send, `originalHandleChecked: true`, zero foreign-handle/overlapping
  polls, private preparation through the sanctioned launcher path, current ownership in-record
  (§17.7 for M/L/R/B; §17.10, §17.14.1 for I0/I1/N). **F and BG are fail-closed NON-ADJUDICABLE for
  Gate A**: their evidence collection did not complete, so `route.actual: null` and the
  linkage/launch/send/handle facts are all null (§17.12, §17.14.2) — no Gate A claim is made for them
  in either direction. **RV/AR/ST are the root family** (`mode: "root"`): Gate A's rescue-Child
  route-`named`/launch-send/handle conjuncts are not applicable to that surface (RV carried launch 1 /
  send 0), and those commands' standing rests on §17.14.3's own per-command bases, never on Gate A's
  Child-route clause.
- **Gate B (long discriminator / repeat): NOT FULLY PASSED — fail-closed `inconclusive`.** Every
  discriminator clause passed per arm (M nonterminal-measured; L and R each ≥ M+30000 remaining with
  attributable natural observations beyond M, on proven-identical settings), but the exact-terminal
  linkage clause is UNESTABLISHED on every record (merged-stream limitation), so the exported repeat
  verdict is `inconclusive` and the gate's no-unknown-evidence clause fails closed (§17.5, §17.7,
  §17.8 item 1).

  B under matched cap/exec-default/worker/budget/model; fewer measured observation re-entries under the
  candidate (1 vs 7, oracle `reduced` both arms); Root joins counted separately; no token or
  whole-job-zero claim (§17.6–17.7).

  interrupts BEFORE any attributable pending child poll existed, with unclassified 23-char targets
  (`exactTargetMatch: null`, `orderingBound: false`); the ONE approved successor F changed the turn

### 18.6 Scoped adoption decision: **do-not-adopt-yet**

**The candidate long-wait policy is NOT adopted — not into any production default, user configuration,
canonical Skill, Role template or marketplace snapshot — by this branch, this report, or the research
PR merge.** Human adoption and a separately authorized production change remain required for anything
to change; no production default was changed by executing this plan.

The three measured blockers, named precisely:

1. **Gate D is mandatory for an affirmative managed-Rescue recommendation and is BLOCKED at every
   layer.** Native interruption could not be attributed on any of the three interrupt runs: the
   unknown-call/unclassified-cell fail-closed retention design (23-char suppressed targets on I0/I1;
   the 80-byte unclassified script cell on F) leaves delivery observability — and therefore
   responsiveness, settlement and no-collateral qualification — unestablishable on this evidence path.
2. **Gate B's exact-output clause is unproven.** The pinned unified-exec serialization merges
   stdout/stderr, so exact terminal byte/exit linkage is unestablished on every record and the repeat
   verdict is `inconclusive` fail-closed — regardless of the passed discriminators.
3. **RV (Review) is unqualified and blocks a BROAD shared-default deployment.** The numeric
   outer-default half of the candidate is host-global host config with no supported Role-scoped
   override: raising it reaches Root-owned Review (whose no-send early exit is a production-scope
   question, untouched here) and every other code-mode consumer. Only the waiting-PARAGRAPH half is
   isolable (a per-Role template artifact with explicit per-call windows), and even that surface
   inherits blockers 1–2 for the managed-Rescue recommendation itself.

Smallest scoped next actions (each a bounded follow-up requiring its own authorization — NOT a new
generic feasibility campaign, and nothing here implies the research PR merge enables production):

- **Native-interruption delivery observability**: close the unknown-call/unclassified-cell evidence
  gap (a bounded structural admission for the observed cell shapes, preserving the privacy/retention
  design) so a future authorized interrupt run can establish exact delivery attribution — the one gap
  that blocked every Gate D layer.
- **An exact-output stream-attribution seam**: an attributable stdout-only capture (or equivalent
  supported mechanism) so Gate B's exact-terminal linkage clause can be measured instead of failing
  closed on merged streams.
- **The Review no-send cause as a separate production scope**: RV's early exit predates this campaign,
  is not a shell-waiting failure, and needs separate implementation authority — it is recorded, not
  fixed here.

If and only if those produce the missing evidence under fresh authorization, the decision can be
revisited per surface (the §17.14.5 blast-radius matrix is the scope map); nothing in this report
lowers any §8 gate or carries a blanket family inference.

### 19.3 Stdout-only seam: no supported split-stream capture exists; the passive fallback is selected and transport-tested (checkbox 3)

**(a) The existing-supported-capture investigation closes NEGATIVE, at exact source lines.** At pin
`dffa0deb` the managed-Child exec path merges stdout and stderr BEFORE any observation surface:
`codex_utils_pty` spawns the command with separate stdout/stderr receivers
(`SpawnedPty { stdout_rx, stderr_rx }`, `core/src/unified_exec/process.rs:355-362`), then
`combine_output_receivers` (`codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process.rs:320-344`) interleaves both into ONE
broadcast channel by arrival order with no stream labels; the combined chunks feed a single
`OutputBuffers` pair of head+tail buffers (`process.rs:45-56`, one pending + one transcript buffer,
bound `UNIFIED_EXEC_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`); the completion event then reports `stdout` = the merged
transcript and `stderr` = LITERALLY EMPTY (`emit_exec_end_for_unified_exec`,
`core/src/unified_exec/async_watcher.rs:344-352`: `stdout: StreamOutput::new(aggregated_output.clone())`,
`stderr: StreamOutput::new(String::new())`), and the streaming deltas are all labeled `Stdout`
(`async_watcher.rs:309-317`; `ExecOutputStream::Stderr` appears NOWHERE under
`core/src/unified_exec/`). The failure path likewise folds stderr into the aggregate
(`async_watcher.rs:395-413`). This is the exact structural cause behind §17.8 item 1 and §18.6
blocker 2, now pinned to source lines: **there is no supported split-stream capture on the actual
managed-Child path to reuse.** (Stream-labeled surfaces exist only in OTHER subsystems the Rescue
launcher never traverses — app-server `command_exec`, exec-server, plain `exec.rs` — and rerouting
the launcher through them would change the production entrypoint/business flow, which is prohibited.)

**(b) The selected seam: a fixture-only Node preload, passive stdout tee, exactly-scoped.** The
launcher is the terminal writer's process: `skills/rescue/launcher.mjs` (installed realpath, argv
exactly `['invoke-prepared','rescue']` — launcher.mjs:11-18, :21-28, :30-35) imports and executes
`runCompanionCli` (zcode-companion.mjs:2722), which on success writes
`formatDirectInvocationSuccess(output).text` to stdout (zcode-companion.mjs:2743, :2751) and on
failure writes `formatDirectInvocationError(error).text` with the bounded exit code (:2761-2768;
JOB_INTERRUPTED keeps empty stdout + bounded stderr + signal exit :2761-2766). The stdout/stderr/exit
contract is `scripts/lib/direct-invocation-result.mjs` (whole module), framing is `render.mjs`
(:28-56), and the freeze treats `render.mjs` as authoritative. The preload gates on (1) fixture-only
env vars being present, (2) `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` equaling the fixture-declared installed
launcher realpath, (3) `process.argv.slice(2)` strictly `['invoke-prepared','rescue']` — and is
INERT in every other process. On match it tees every `process.stdout.write` chunk (string with
explicit/default encoding, or Buffer) to one private capture file (`wx`, mode 0600, one capture per
fixture nonce), delegates the ORIGINAL write call through unchanged (same arguments, same return
value, same callback dispatch), and records at process exit a bounded meta record: captureComplete,
truncated, byteCount, **captureSha256** (the SHA-256 of the captured stdout bytes, computed AT
CAPTURE CLOSE by the preload over exactly the bytes it wrote — satisfying plan §3's "byte
count/digest"), maxBytes 65536, exitCode (`process.exitCode ?? 0`), argv, entryRealpath, durationMs.
The exact-output oracle consumes this capture-time digest (plus the capture bytes/byteCount, which
the read-side module re-verifies against the digest before use) — Task 2 does not re-decide where
the digest comes from. Bytes beyond 64 KiB set `truncated: true` and the capture stays INCOMPLETE —
a truncated capture can never pass the exact-match oracle (fail closed, never a partial
expectation). The capture file lives only in the fixture-owned nonce directory, is never written
inside the repository or any record, and is disposed with the fixture; preparation
markers/capabilities/auth NEVER enter it (only terminal stdout bytes do, by construction of the
argv gate).

### 19.4 Host target/activity event persistence and join rules at the pin (checkbox 4)

Source trace at `dffa0deb` (read-only `git show`; citations exact):

- `handle_interrupt_agent` (`core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/interrupt_agent.rs:37-77`):
  resolves the target (`resolve_agent_target`, :46), dispatches `agent_control.interrupt(...)`
  (:49-55), snapshots `previous_status` (:61 — a PRE-dispatch status, returned as the tool result
  :76), then emits `SubAgentActivityItem { id: call_id, agent_thread_id, agent_path, kind:
  Interrupted }` (:62-74). **Emission is strictly AFTER the dispatch returns** — its timestamps bound
  the dispatch from above and are never the dispatch instant.
- `emit_sub_agent_activity` (`core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2.rs:44-52`) wraps the item as
  `TurnItem::SubAgentActivity` and emits turn-item STARTED + COMPLETED events;
  `emit_turn_item_started/completed` (`core/src/session/mod.rs:2714-2771`) send
  `EventMsg::ItemStarted/ItemCompleted` with `started_at_ms`/`completed_at_ms`;
  `send_event` → `send_event_raw` (persist = true, mod.rs:2441, :2635-2637) persists
  `RolloutItem::EventMsg` into rollout storage (mod.rs:2684-2686).
- **Persistence policy decides retention** (`codex-rs/rollout/src/policy.rs`):
  `EventMsg::ItemStarted` is TRANSIENT (never persisted, :212); `ItemCompleted` persists through
  `persisted_item_completed_event` (:218-268) — in **Paginated** history mode EVERY item kind is
  kept (`_ => Cow::Borrowed`, :281) including `TurnItem::SubAgentActivity` of kind `Interrupted`;
  in **Legacy** mode only `FunctionCallOutput | Plan | Extension(Sleep)` and
  `SubAgentActivity(kind == Completed)` survive (:226-237). The separate legacy
  `EventMsg::SubAgentActivity` event persists only in Legacy mode and only for kind != Completed
  (:156-158).
- **The installed CLI's local store defaults to PAGINATED:**
  `ThreadHistoryMode`'s enum default is `Legacy` (`protocol/src/protocol.rs:883-890`), but the
  `LocalThreadStore` override returns `Paginated` (`codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/mod.rs:481-484`;
  trait default Legacy with the stated compatibility rationale, `thread-store/src/store.rs:134-140`),
  the mode rides the thread's SessionMeta
  (`canonical_history_mode_from_rollout_items`, `thread-store/src/types.rs:142-153`), and a spawned
  V2 Child inherits its PARENT's mode (Paginated only when the parent is Paginated,
  `core/src/agent/control/spawn.rs:823-827`). Source conclusion: on installed local storage at this
  pin, Root AND Child rollouts are Paginated by default and the host-generated Interrupted activity
  IS durably retained. **Source presence is still not an installed observation**: the fixture-owned
  confirmation (reading the actual Root rollout for the actual item in a registered trial) is
  registered as the FIRST verification step of any future live interrupt case; no claim about
  installed behavior is made from source alone.
- **Durable wire shape** (serde tags verified): a rollout line
  `{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":<ROOT thread>,"turn_id":<root
  turn>,"item":{"type":"SubAgentActivity","model":…,"reasoning_effort":…,"id":"<interrupt call_id>","kind":"interrupted","agent_thread_id":"<child thread id>","agent_path":"<v2 path>"},"started_at_ms":…|absent,"completed_at_ms":…}}`
  (`RolloutItemWire`, `history/src/rollout_payload.rs:33-63`; `EventMsg` tag
  `type`+snake_case, protocol.rs:1463-1467; `TurnItem` tag `type` without rename — Rust variant
  names, `protocol/src/items.rs:46-89`; `SubAgentActivityItem` fields items.rs:368-375;
  `ItemCompletedEvent` with optional `started_at_ms` and `completed_at_ms`, protocol.rs:2060-2074;
  `SubAgentActivityKind` snake_case with `Interrupted`, protocol.rs:4502-4509). The spawn
  acknowledgement joins through the SAME item family: the spawn path emits
  Started/Completed activity items through the same `emit_sub_agent_activity`, so
  `agent_thread_id`/`agent_path` are shared identity across spawn and interrupt items.
- **The actual finite shape missing from available fixture-owned evidence** (the registration target):
  this host-generated `event_msg`/`item_completed`/`SubAgentActivity(kind=interrupted)` payload. The
  current evidence reader admits only the CALL side — `extractInterruptInteraction`
  (evidence.mjs:1722+) parses the interrupt tool call (family, callId, scrubbed target,
  `callAtMs`/`notBeforeMs`/`notAfterMs` attributable bounds, poll-interval machinery :1611-1618) and
  has NO admission for event-msg SubAgentActivity payloads (zero matches). That absence — not a new
  regex — is the gap Task 3 closes, plus the two withheld-shape facts of §19.2.

**Supported admission set (registered BEFORE any live trial; every conjunct required):** (1) exactly
ONE `interrupt_agent` call in the owning Root rollout (`callCount: 1`, the existing contract);
(2) exactly ONE matching host activity item with `kind == "interrupted"` whose `id` equals that
call's id (direct call-id join — never alias text, never caller-supplied strings relabeled
authoritative); (3) the item's `agent_thread_id` equals the pending Child's exact id as returned by
the spawn acknowledgement (the record's `linkage.childThreadId` namespace); (4) the item occurs in
the OWNING ROOT's rollout (its `thread_id` is the Root's), ordered strictly inside the confirmed
pending window [attributable poll start, resolution) and before natural completion; (5) the item is
timed (`completed_at_ms` finite and positive; untimed items keep timing unestablished, never zero);
(6) the delivered interrupt's `previous_status` remains a pre-dispatch snapshot only, never
settlement. **Counterexamples (each fails the layer, no fallback interaction):** activity item
absent (Legacy-mode rollout, older binary, or truncated rollout) → delivery identity unestablished;
`kind` Started/Completed or any other value; `agent_thread_id` matching a sibling/unrelated/self
agent; duplicate activity items for one call id; id join missing or ambiguous; item ordered outside
the pending window or after settlement; untimed item treated as timed; activity item WITHOUT a
pending observation (emission alone proves nothing about turn/cell settlement — host activity proves
dispatch identity ONLY, never cancellation/Companion/job settlement); a Root final message, gate
release or cleanup fact offered as the activity item. Emission-after-dispatch timestamps bound
timing (dispatch ≤ completed_at_ms); they are never read as the dispatch instant and never as
settlement latency endpoints by themselves — §19.6's basis rules apply.

### 19.5 Durable-job identity/obligation predicates and the adapter side-effect classification (checkbox 5)

**Layout identity (the exact fixture-owned partition only).** One workspace partition =
`<dataRoot>/workspaces/<sha256(realpath(workspace))>/` (`resolveWorkspaceStorage`,
scripts/lib/workspace.mjs:11-45 — workspaceKey is the SHA-256 of the workspace REALPATH; symlinks or
non-canonical paths resolve to a different partition or fail). Partition contents on the attached
foreground path: `jobs/<64-hex>.json` (+ per-job log), `job-owners/index.json` + per-owner binding
entries (`[64-hex].json`, bounded, state.mjs readOwnedJobs), `.state.lock/` (advisory flock
directory), plus the other stores (`active-turns/`, `callers/`, `broker/`, `cancel-attempts/`,
`cancel-attempt-locks/`, `cancel-locks/`, `sessions/`, `session-locks/`, rescue-preparation store,
rescue-binding partition). Job identity = 64-hex id + `workspace` realpath equality +
ownerSessionId/ownerTurnId + `command: 'rescue'` + `readOnly: false` for THIS path
(`makeReservedJob`, state.mjs:1537-1556; validators state.mjs:3018-3038). Only this fixture-owned
partition is ever enumerated, under hard entry/byte bounds — never real user plugin data, never
latest-job guessing.

**Adapter side-effect classification (the supposedly read-only readers are NOT passive):**

- `createStateStore().readJob(workspace, jobId)` (state.mjs:1078-1087): `jobStorage` →
  `ensurePrivateDirectoryWithin` for `jobs/` AND `job-owners/` (state.mjs:1479-1494 → fs.mjs:51-74,
  which mkdir(0700) AND chmod(0700) every component even on EEXIST) → `withFileLock` →
  **creates directories and takes the exclusive advisory lock. NOT passive.**
- `listJobs` (:1090) same construction; `listOwnedJobs` (:1103) additionally `ensureOwnerIndex`
  (:2684, creates the index). `peekOwnedJobs` (:1126-1138) is lock-FREE but still calls `jobStorage`
  — **it creates/chmods the layout even though it never locks.** "Lock-free" is not "passive".
- `resolveWorkspaceStorage` itself (workspace.mjs:38-43) `ensurePrivateDirectory` × 3 (dataRoot,
  `workspaces/`, key dir) — create/chmod.
- `withFileLock` (fs.mjs:256-380): the lock is a DIRECTORY `<lockPath>/advisory.lock` file held by a
  native fd lock (`tryLock`/`unlock`, :324, :361 — released by unlock+close, NEVER unlinked, so lock
  files persist); default `createLayout: true` creates the 0700/0600 layout (:275, :307,
  `ensureLockLayout` :383+); `createLayout: false` opens and validates a PRE-EXISTING private layout
  without creating or chmodding (:280-281, :300-304) — the lock-free-reading precedent inside the
  production code.
- The PURE read primitives (verified no-write): `readJsonFile`/`readBoundedJsonFile` (fs.mjs:227,
  :103 — no-follow final symlink, declared-size rejection, bound+1 reads), `readJobRecord` +
  `validateJobRecord` (state.mjs:3000-3015, :3141), `readPrivateDirectory` (fs.mjs:81-94, before/
  after identity checks), `readOwnedJobs` (state.mjs, `readPrivateDirectory` +
  `readBoundedJsonFile`, ENOENT → []), and the private complete-layout resolver
  `existingJobStorageForRepair` (state.mjs:1507-1525: lstat every path, no symlink, directory, mode
  0700, realpath equality, fail-closed — resolves a complete pre-existing layout WITHOUT creating or
  chmodding; module-private).
- Lifecycle/reconciliation adapters on this path are writers by design: `stopAndSettle`
  (rescue-lifecycle.mjs:154-195) persists the durable stop intent FIRST (no stop intent may exist
  unless a real stop authority acted — `stopCauseFor` :114-122 grants authority ONLY to explicit
  stop intent, matching-epoch SessionEnd receipts, or attached-foreground host-coordination loss,
  :126-140), then runner cleanup (`runRunnerCleanup` :459-471, gated by `cleanupAllowsSettlement`
  :485-487), then winner election (natural success first; uncertain outcomes RETAIN the writable
  guard, `unresolved-stop`); `reconcileRescueChildForPreparation` runs on PREPARE, never on
  interrupt (§16.2 boundary unchanged).

**Frozen obligation predicates for THIS attached foreground path (production-defined only):**

1. **Job-record terminality**: winner ∈ `TERMINAL` = {succeeded, failed, cancelled}
   (recovery.mjs:18) published in the exact job record; `cancelling` is a RETAINED GUARD, not a
   terminal state.
2. **Stop-intent presence**: `validStopIntent(job.stopIntent)` (rescue-binding.mjs STOP_INTENT
   validators, version 1) — for a foreign-origin native interrupt NO durable stop intent exists
   (§16.2), and its presence would be evidence of a REAL stop authority, never assumed.
3. **Executor/runner cleanup duty**: `isMarkedRunnerClaim(job)` (recovery.mjs:237-240) = writable
   rescue + marked runner-format version + digest `workerLeaseId` + safe positive `childPid`; a
   terminal record STILL CARRYING the marked claim has an OUTSTANDING local termination duty
   (recovery.mjs:148-158: terminal + marked claim + raw-record projection ⇒ NOT settled;
   `runner-cleanup-pending` ⇒ NOT settled; a freed lease proves the runner gone, never the process
   tree — recovery.mjs:202-216) — so **a terminal status alone is NOT proof that executor/cleanup
   duties are discharged**.
4. **SessionEnd-receipt obligations**: `discoverSessionEndObligations` (recovery.mjs:185-229) —
   terminal-with-marked-claim and nonterminal writable/read-only-detached records, epoch-scoped;
   `endedObligationSettled` (:148-158) is the exported discharge predicate; `cancelling` settles
   only WITH a valid persisted stop intent.
5. **Writable exclusion**: a nonterminal writable rescue job holds the workspace's writable guard
   (`WRITABLE_JOB_EXISTS`, state.mjs:1539-1543) — "guard retained" is the SAFE unresolved state, not
   a failure of settlement and never readable as success.
6. **Binding currency**: the rescue-binding partition (`RESCUE_BINDING_VERSION` 3, bounded record/
   partition sizes, rescue-binding.mjs:11-20) decides resumability's `bindingCurrent` conjunct
   (§19.3(d)); a stale/advanced binding is unproven, never false-by-guess.

**Passive snapshot strategy (the Task 2 reader contract; a hardcoded-null placeholder is NOT
implementation):** resolve the partition exactly as `existingJobStorageForRepair` does (pure lstat
chain, no symlink, 0700, realpath equality — any incompleteness fails closed to `unknown`, never
mkdir); read the exact bound job via the production bounded read + `validateJobRecord` contract;
evaluate obligations with the EXPORTED production predicates (`endedObligationSettled`,
`isMarkedRunnerClaim`, `discoverSessionEndObligations` semantics, `resumableJobIndicator`); NEVER
acquire any lock (a held lock is observed as `unknown — concurrent writer possible`, never probed,
never waited on); snapshot directory entries, file contents and modes before AND after every read
pass and require equality (proving no mkdir/chmod/new lock/stop intent/state update by the reader
itself); a missing record is recorded `missing`, never successful cleanup. **Documented consistency
limits:** per-file reads are atomic but the CROSS-FILE snapshot is not — a concurrent writer can
produce a torn multi-file view, so each observation carries its per-layer basis and any detected
before/after inequality or cross-file contradiction marks the affected layers `unknown` (null stays
null; null never becomes zero or not-applicable without a demonstrated path reason); aggregates are
`settled` ONLY when ALL applicable duties are POSITIVELY established; partial observations remain
per-layer facts and are never folded into Companion or terminal-stdout outcomes.

  contradictory; the §16.5 freeze stands unmodified). Prior interrupt runs (I0/I1/F) never produced
  an attributable delivery, so the bound remains REGISTERED-BUT-NOT-YET-APPLICABLE, exactly as
  §17.10.3/§18.1 recorded; Task 4/5 apply it only after Task 3's admission set (§19.4) is satisfied
  on a live record.

  (`held-turn-monotonic-elapsed-ms`, driver.mjs — the F record's
  `held.timeline.pollStartedAtElapsedMs: 72069` is THIS clock) for all probe-side events; (2)
  attributable rollout event timestamps (epoch ms; `interruptEventTimestampMs` evidence.mjs:1136-1146
  accepts the ISO/finite-positive shapes only) for host-side events; (3) the attributable
  original-handle poll timeline (`observations.pollStartedAtElapsedMs`, null on F — a DIFFERENT field
  from the held timeline, §19.2 item 3). **Join rules:** delivery-to-settlement latency is computed
  ONLY when both endpoints carry attributable positions in ONE established ordering
  (`callAtMs`/`responseAtMs` poll intervals, evidence.mjs:1611-1618, or the bound machinery
  `notBeforeMs`/`notAfterMs`); a host-emission timestamp that cannot be joined keeps the latency
  `null`/unestablished (`timingBasis: "unavailable"`), never an approximation, never zero. The new
  §19.4 activity item's `completed_at_ms` is an EMISSION timestamp that bounds dispatch from above;
  it may serve as a delivery bound or an ordering fact, never as the dispatch instant and never
  alone as a latency endpoint.
- **Layer separation retained verbatim:** the turn/cell/poll responsiveness bound NEVER absorbs the
  Companion outcome, the durable job/guard layers, or the no-collateral control — the oracle's
  reasons and layer flags keep them separate (release-qualification.mjs:837-890); unknown aggregate
  job-settlement bounds remain EXPLICIT (production has NO aggregate delivery-to-settlement deadline —
  §16.5's composition table stands; no new production deadline is created by this registration).
- **Natural completion is never cancelled:** an observed natural completion reported as `cancelled`
  is a misclassification that BLOCKS the settlement (`natural-completion-misclassified-as-cancelled`,
  release-qualification.mjs:864-866); a natural terminal winner that settles after an interrupt is
  recorded as natural (§16.2/§18.5), never relabeled.
- **Cleanup boundary:** observations that count toward native/natural credit must COMPLETE before the
  safety-cleanup boundary; cleanup-side facts (`processTermination`, budget kills, fixture disposal)
  remain cleanup facts (`nativeInterruptionClaimed: false` discipline, §17 records) and can never
  seed native settlement. The survival control's ~80-second readiness floor (§16.4 revision) remains
  an OBSERVER-COORDINATION approximation ONLY — never a pending acknowledgment, never a Child-poll
  observation.

before settlement (codex round 5)` failed with "the partial lifecycle trio invalidates the

(3) **Persisted stop intents reported on natural terminal winners** — the stopIntent projection

(4) **The fence uses the read's OWN completion time, not the join time** — ONE complete fence,
implemented exactly to this contract:
  - `startDurableSnapshotRead` (driver.mjs :1874-1915) wraps the read AT START: a `.then` carrier
    stamps `completedAtMs` (Date.now — the same wall clock as `cleanupBoundaryAtMs`) at the

    await; the carrier instant (not an attached field) is the fence input.
  - Earliest cleanup boundary = the FIRST `cleanupBoundaryAtMs` ever recorded on the held cleanup

    completed (`completedAtMs` set by the carrier) AND `completedAtMs < earliestBoundaryAtMs`

    flag/signal check plus the budget race).

    `durable-observation-after-cleanup-boundary` block (the budget reason wins if both fire);
    the snapshot's own aggregate stays only as `sampledAggregate`.

**Codex round-7 fixes (2026-10-21; two P2 findings over the round-6 bytes — both pre-existing

(1) **Captures finalized AFTER exit-time stdout writes** — the preload's 'exit' listener was
registered by the preload itself (which loads FIRST through `--require`), so Node's registration-
order emission ran it BEFORE every application exit listener: an application exit handler's
stdout writes reached the terminal AFTER the capture had been closed and its complete meta
published — the bytes were omitted from the admitted capture while the exact-linkage verdict
stayed `matched: true` (repro `result\n` + exit-handler `extra\n` yielded a complete 7-byte

finalization per the review contract — (a) the read wrapper around `process.reallyExit`
(:257-263): the wrapper publishes the COMPLETE meta (SHA-256 over ALL captured bytes) at
reallyExit time, which `process.exit` reaches only AFTER every 'exit' listener returned; the

**Codex round-11 — PRELOAD STRUCTURAL REWRITE (P1–P5) (2026-10-21; two P2 findings over the
round-10 bytes — BOTH introduced by round-9 changes: the callback-form encoding gap and the
file-derived digest, which also violated the §19.3 freeze "captureSha256 computed at capture
close over exactly the bytes written". The capture preload had been patched across rounds 7-11
without converging, so the ROOT mandated this STRUCTURAL ENDGAME: closurePreloadSource
REWRITTEN against the complete specification below, with a matrix suite. This is the final
deferral under the repeat-failure ladder — a round-12 fix-introduced capture-family finding
hands the file to a fresh fixer under this same spec.)**

Spec clauses → implementation (closure-observation.mjs):
- **P1 Gate** (:130-141): active only when the fixture env validates (absolute capture
  directory, 64-hex nonce, absolute declared entry, maxBytes exactly 65536) AND
  `realpathSync(argv[1]) === ENTRY` AND `argv.slice(2)` deep-equals
  `['invoke-prepared','rescue']`; otherwise NOTHING is installed (no listeners, no wrappers, no
  files).
- **P2 Interception** (:164-263): the write wrapper computes the DELIVERED bytes for EVERY call
  form — Buffer/TypedArray as-is; string through the explicit encoding if a string, ELSE the
  tracked default encoding (`defaultEncoding`, initial 'utf8', updated by wrapping
  `setDefaultEncoding` — covering the round-9 finding-1 gap AND its callback form
  (:208-215)); feeds those bytes to the AUTHORITATIVE running SHA-256 hasher and appends them to
  the wx 0600 capture file under the 64 KiB cap (exceeding sets `truncated`); forwards the
  ORIGINAL arguments unchanged (return value/callback/errors untouched); a capture-side fs error
  names `captureError` and stops capturing without altering delivery; `byteCount` = bytes
  hashed; the file is NEVER read back for the digest.
- **P3 Finalization** (:198-232, :266-284): last-writer-wins meta at two idempotent points —
  the 'exit' listener (registered at install; `beforeExit` re-orders it to the END of the
  listener list) and the `process.reallyExit` wrapper (authoritative last word on explicit
  exits). No forced exit, no exitCode mutation. Closed meta field set:
  `{version, nonce, entryRealpath, argv, byteCount, captureSha256 (hash.copy().digest() at that
  instant), truncated, maxBytes, exitCode, finalizedBy, finalizations,
  writesAfterFinalization, captureError?, durationMs}` — published 'wx' first, republished 'w';
  a write after any finalization increments `writesAfterFinalization`, still appends+hashes, and
  immediately republishes (an INVALIDATED meta carries its named reason through every
  republication and is never resurrected).
- **P4 Admission** (validateCaptureMeta :413-443 + admitStdoutCapture :489-580): the closed
  field set is enforced (`captureComplete` DERIVED, never published); complete only when
  captureError null ∧ !truncated ∧ `writesAfterFinalization === 0` ∧ file size === byteCount ∧
  sha256(fileBytes) === captureSha256 (the FILE verified against the hasher-authoritative
  digest — tamper → the named `capture-digest-mismatch`, renaming the retired
  `capture-sha256-mismatch`) ∧ meta.exitCode === handle-linked exit (else
  `capture-exit-code-mismatch`); the meta nonce is bound to the queried nonce
  (`capture-meta-nonce-mismatch`); everything else keeps its named status.
- **P5 Matrix**: the table-driven suite below.

Matrix results (form × default encoding — delivered bytes == captured bytes == hashed digest;

c3a9): buffer/string/string+cb under latin1 → e9 rows (named capture-utf8-invalid with

**SLICE A — the §19.4 missing finite shape, implemented in the existing bounded parser.**
`admitInterruptHostDelivery(rollouts, interaction, options)` (evidence.mjs, after
`extractInterruptInteraction`) admits ONLY the registered host-generated delivery item: an
`event_msg`/`item_completed` payload whose `item` is a `SubAgentActivity` of kind `interrupted`
(persistence chain per §19.4: interrupt_agent.rs:62-74 → emit_sub_agent_activity → ItemCompleted;
ItemStarted is TRANSIENT and never scanned; Paginated retention per policy.rs:218-268/:281). No new
grammar, no lost-body inference, no raw-body retention: unsupported shapes fail closed with their
structural diagnostics preserved (per-conjunct facts + counts + named reasons survive; the
interaction facts and every unrelated observation are never erased). The registered six-conjunct
set maps to the named counterexample reasons: `host-activity-call-count-not-one` (conjunct 1);
conjunct 2's direct call-id join in the OWNING ROOT's rollout only —
`host-activity-item-absent` / `host-activity-kind-not-interrupted` (Started/Completed/any other
kind with the call id, the multi_agents_v2.rs:44-52 family) / `host-activity-id-join-missing` /
`host-activity-duplicate-item` / `host-activity-foreign-rollout` (a same-shaped copy in the Child's
or any third rollout is NEVER a duplicate of the root item); conjunct 3 —
`host-activity-agent-thread-mismatch` / `host-activity-child-identity-unestablished`; conjunct 4 —
`host-activity-foreign-rollout` / `host-activity-owning-root-unestablished` /
`host-activity-without-pending-observation` / `host-activity-outside-pending-window` /
`host-activity-after-settlement` / `host-activity-window-unestablished` (an observed window with an
unestablishable attributable start stays unestablished, never approximated); conjunct 5 —
`host-activity-untimed` (`completed_at_ms` finite POSITIVE only; the pinned deserialization default
0 — protocol.rs `default_item_completed_at_ms` for old rollouts — and absent stamps are UNTIMED,
never zero); delivery-state guards `host-activity-delivery-rejected` /
`host-activity-delivery-unobserved`; `host-activity-no-attempted-call` (null admission, never a
fabricated negative); `host-activity-item-bound-exceeded` (the 64-item scan bound). Conjunct 6 is a
NON-consumption discipline: the admission never reads `previous_status` at all (the pinned
PRE-dispatch snapshot, interrupt_agent.rs:61/:76) — pipeline-proven by the admission succeeding
while every settlement field stays null on a snapshot-only record. Emission-after-dispatch
discipline: `completed_at_ms` is an ordering fact inside the confirmed pending window
([attributable poll start, resolution), before natural completion), never the dispatch instant,
never a latency endpoint (§19.6). The interaction gains the ADDITIVE `callId` field (the last
interrupt-shaped call's host-assigned id — the join key; a shared-cell interrupt carries its CELL's
call id, exactly what the host emits). The registered parser behaviors were all pipeline-proven
UNDER the admission: raw directive validity/preservation (the interrupt statement inside a
three-statement supported cell with leading/trailing foreign statements — the whole-cell fail-closed
grammar untouched, the cell's call id the join key, the statement's own result position resolving
the delivery, the bounded execution-time attribution intact), explicit terminate mixed with native
cancel (sequential observations — the native cancellation of the interrupted observation credited,
the later new observation's explicit ender separately classified, the admission independent of both),
resolved-cell reuse and cross-session identical ids (the foreign-copy counterexample; the child-side
poll interval machinery untouched).
